history.dynasty: Kachwaha (patronage of Maharaja Madho Singh I)
history.summary: The temple was built under the supervision of Seth Jai Ram Paliwal, who brought the Ganesha idol here in 1761 while accompanying Maharaja Madho Singh I from Udaipur; the idol itself is said to be over 500 years old and to have originally come from Gujarat. Legend says the King of Mewar carted the idol on a bullock cart and vowed to build a temple wherever the cart first stopped — it stopped at the foot of Moti Dungri ('pearl hill'). The sindoor-coloured Ganesha idol is distinctive for its trunk curving to the right. The complex is built in the Nagara style, modelled on a Scottish castle, using limestone and marble with fine lattice work; the adjoining fort-palace remains the private residence of the royal family and is not open to visitors. (Note: sources disagree on whether construction took four years or four months; the 1761 completion date is consistent.)

name: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is the 'Pink City' — founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, its rose-hued walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the historic heart of Kachwaha Rajput culture, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 11 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur railway station area about 4 km away (verify); Gandhi Nagar station is the nearest halt per some sources.
travel.road: On Moti Dungri Road near JLN Marg, Tilak Nagar; reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Wednesdays and Ganesh Chaturthi are the most festive but crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:30 AM-1:30 PM and evening 4:30 PM-9:00 PM (sources vary; mangala aarti at 4:00 AM — verify).
